Commentary.Commentary: Back for the chase! Both umpires are out in the middle again, followed by the players of the United Arab Emirates. Also, walk out the two openers of India where Abhishek Sharma has a new opening partner in the vice-captain, Shubman Gill. Haider Ali has the new ball in his hands, and he will start the proceedings. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

And what about the United Arab Emirates’ batting? Nothing more to say. After reaching 42/1 decently in the Powerplay, they simply lost the plot. Skipper Waseem tried to anchor but failed, and the rest offered no fight at all - soft dismissals, poor shot selection, and no partnerships. Only both openers managed to get into double digits, which tells you about their batting story. Did the toss decision work? Absolutely. Surya’s call to bowl first was a masterstroke, and now India need just 58 to chase. With this kind of dominance, the second innings might be over before the United Arab Emirates blink. The chase is about to begin, so don't go anywhere.

Numerous records have been broken in the first inning, as this has been that kind of performance from both teams. So, what did India do with their bowling? They came in with fire. Jasprit Bumrah set the tone early with a searing yorker to dismiss Alishan Sharafu, while Varun Chakaravarthy chipped in as well during the Powerplay. Then came Kuldeep Yadav, in the ninth over, he took three wickets in six balls that broke the United Arab Emirates’ back. Shivam Dube’s clever variations added three more in the latter part of the inning, and Axar Patel kept the choke going when he got a chance. Every bowler contributed, making it a near-perfect performance with the ball for them.

RECKLESS? UNDER PRESSURE? What should we call this lacklustre batting display from the United Arab Emirates? But on the other side, India have been CLINICAL, blowing away their opposition for a mere total of just 57, after electing to bowl first. It was some ruthless, relentless, and razor-sharp bowling in Dubai. A demolition job from the defending champions, who hunted in packs and gave the batters no breathing space. Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates’s batting was timid and fell apart like a house of cards after a promising start. In the end, it looked like a one-sided show that has left the crowd stunned at how quickly the innings crumbled.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Kuldeep Yadav wraps things in style, finishing with a 4-for. He floats it fuller and slides the ball in and around off. It lands and then spins just a shy bit away from the batter. Haider Ali draws his front foot out and tries to push it to the off side, but he plays over the line and the ball sneaks between the gap of bat and pad, just taking a bit of feather of flap of the front pad, passing close to the inside edge. Sanju Samson does the rest behind the stumps. There is an appeal from the Indians, seemingly for the LBW, and the umpire raises his finger up. Now, there is total confusion in between as Ali walks up to Rohid to have a chat. And hang on, this is given caught behind. But since UAE have burnt all their reviews, they cannot go upstairs. Haider makes his way to the dugout eventually. UNITED ARAB EMIRATES HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT ON 57!

And oh, there is an appeal for a run out as Sanju Samson releases an underarm throw at the batting end, and scores the direct hit. The square leg umpire has referred it upstairs. There is no bat involved for being caught behind. Now, onto the run out check. The third umpire confirms that there is nothing behind the popping crease, and he deems that Junaid is marginally short of his crease. But the skipper of India, Suryakumar Yadav, withdraws his appeal after OUT loads on the giant screen and Junaid Siddique doesn't walk out. Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Jasprit Bumrah to Alishan Sharafu, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length but around leg, Alishan Sharafu looks to sway away at first and then looks to play an upper cut in the end but he misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Jasprit Bumrah to Alishan Sharafu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches it up, slower and just outside off, Alishan Sharafu uses his feet but he has to adjust his shot due to the lack of pace on it and ends up driving it to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Jasprit Bumrah to Alishan Sharafu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length, over off, angling in from wide of the crease, Alishan Sharafu watches it carefully and gets on top of the bounce before dabbing it into the deck and the ball rolls away into the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Jasprit Bumrah to Alishan Sharafu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Both openers are off the mark now! Full and angling in, around leg, Muhammad Waseem gets his front leg forward and tickles it to deep fine leg for a single to get off the mark.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Jasprit Bumrah to Muhammad Waseem, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Spin or pace? The latter. Here's Jasprit Bumrah into the attack from the far end.
Nagging length and outside off, dabbed down to backward point off the back foot. A good start for United Arab Emirates as 11 runs come off the first over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Hardik Pandya to Alishan Sharafu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A MISFIELD AND A BOUNDARY MORE! Short of a length and outside off, shaping away. Alishan Sharafu goes deep in his crease and throws his hands at it. Gets it sliced off the outer half of the bat and the ball goes uppishly towards deep third. Varun Chakaravarthy sprints across to his right and even puts in a dive, but makes a mess of it and the ball goes over the ropes.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Hardik Pandya to Alishan Sharafu, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: EDGED AND FOUR! A lucky boundary for Alishan Sharafu. On a length and outside off, shapingAlishan Sharafu charges down the track and looks to loft it over covers. Only manages to get a thick outside edge as the ball goes over the leaping first slip fielder for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Hardik Pandya to Alishan Sharafu, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and over the top of the off stump, Alishan Sharafu uses his feet but gets cramped and due to an extra bounce. He adjusts his shot and chops it out towards extra cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Hardik Pandya to Alishan Sharafu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, angling in from wide of the crease and then gets it to move away, around middle, Alishan Sharafu gets behind the line of the ball and defends it towards mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Hardik Pandya to Alishan Sharafu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: United Arab Emirates and Alishan Sharafu are underway straightaway! Hardik pitches it up and outside off, getting it to swing away. Alishan prods forward and drives it through the gap between backward point and cover to pick up two runs to open his account. The backward point fielder mops it up.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Hardik Pandya to Alishan Sharafu, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with all pre-match formalities and it is time to get going. A very humid evening in Dubai, as the players make their way to the middle. Not at all a full house, maybe due to the working day, but still, a decent crowd has marked its presence in the stands. SKY leads his men out as the Indian players spread out to their respective fielding positions. Muhammad Waseem and Alishan Sharafu will open for the home side, UAE. And it will be Hardik Pandya to get things underway with the new ball. The countdown is done, and 'Let's Play' says the umpire. Off we go...

Just a few minutes left for the action to get underway here in Dubai. But before that, both sets of players are walking out, followed by the match officials, for the national anthems. It will be the UAE's first, followed by the Indian national anthem.

PITCH REPORT - Sanjay Manjrekar and Russel Arnold are pitchside for their analysis. Russel starts by sharing that it is a bit cooler in terms of heat. Points that there is a shorter boundary with the dimensions being 62 meters and 75 meters on the square. Says the batters will aim to target that shorter boundary. Observes it is rock-hard with a few bare patches as well. Details that it could be slightly two-paced and a bit unpredictable. Sanjay joins in and informs that it is newly-laid pitch. He adds that it is pretty clear to predict from which end the seamers and spinners would operate, as he spots one side being a bit bare and the other being grassy.

India (Playing XI) - Abhishek Sharma, Shubman Gill, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Tilak Varma, Sanju Samson (WK), Shivam Dube, Hardik Pandya, Axar Patel, Kuldeep Yadav, Varun Chakaravarthy, and Jasprit Bumrah.

United Arab Emirates (Playing XI) - Alishan Sharafu, Muhammad Waseem (C), Muhammad Zohaib, Rahul Chopra (WK), Asif Khan, Harshit Kaushik, Dhruv Parashar, Haider Ali, Muhammad Rohid, Junaid Siddique, and Simranjeet Singh.

The skipper of the United Arab Emirates, Muhammad Waseem, says that they were also looking to bowl first as the pitch looks fresh and there might be some movement early on. Reflecting on the recent Tri-Series with Afghanistan and Pakistan, he mentions that the team took a lot of positives and gained confidence from those matches. Adds that today they have different plans, and the focus will be on playing good cricket. Highlights that they are going in with a balanced combination of both spinners and fast bowlers, mixing the experience of seniors with the energy of youngsters.

The captain of India, Suryakumar Yadav, says that it is a fresh wicket and a bit humid as well. Details that due to the weather conditions, there might be dew later on. Tells that they are flexible to do anything. Also highlights that it is just the first game here in the last 3-4 months. Shares that they came to Dubai a few days back and had several good practice sessions, and also a day off. Says everyone is well-prepared and everything looks fine.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favour of India, and the skipper, Suryakumar Yadav, has elected to FIELD first.

So, what can we expect? India are favourites on paper, no question. But the little subplot here is fascinating - India’s selection puzzles, the United Arab Emirates’s rise as giant-slayers, and the Dubai heat that could test even the fittest players. Will it be a straightforward start to India’s campaign, or are the United Arab Emirates about to make the Asia Cup bubble a lot more interesting? The gap is still big, but the United Arab Emirates have shown that they can punch above their weight. With all of that, stay tuned for the toss and team lineups!

And the United Arab Emirates? Are they just here to make up the numbers? Absolutely not. Muhammad Waseem has been leading from the front, smashing runs even against top-ranked sides. Remember, they beat Bangladesh 2-1 earlier this year and nearly shocked Afghanistan last week. Their bowling has teeth too - Muhammad Jawadullah with the new ball, Muhammad Rohid’s left-arm pace, and Junaid Siddique’s experience make them dangerous in home conditions. Add Haider Ali’s in-form left-arm spin, and this team can frustrate even India’s powerful batting. For the United Arab Emirates, the question is - can their batters like Asif Khan, Alishan Sharafu, and Aryansh Sharma handle Bumrah, Arshdeep, and Kuldeep under lights?

What about India? The defending champions look strong, but do they have everything sorted? Not quite. The biggest headache is around selection. Who opens with Abhishek Sharma? All signs point to Shubman Gill, Suryakumar Yadav’s deputy, making his comeback at the top. If Gill opens, where does that leave Sanju Samson? Does he drop to No. 3, move into the middle, or miss out altogether? And what about the gloves? Jitesh Sharma trained long with bat and gloves, so is Samson really on the sidelines? Then there’s the bowling puzzle - four bowlers plus two allrounders, or three plus three? Playing both Kuldeep Yadav and Varun Chakaravarthy together on these sluggish pitches just might be favourable, but if they go with balance, one spinner may have to sit out. These are big calls for Surya and his think tank on night one.

What’s on the menu today? The Asia Cup 2025 finally kicks off for World T20I champions, India, as they meet the United Arab Emirates at the Dubai International Stadium in Dubai. It’s Group A action, where India, Pakistan, the United Arab Emirates, and Oman will battle for two Super Four spots. History? India and the United Arab Emirates have only met once in T20Is - a one-sided affair back in the 2016 Asia Cup. This time, though, the United Arab Emirates arrive with confidence, while India, the eight-time Asia Cup champions, begin their title defence. So, will it be another stroll for India, or can the United Arab Emirates script an early upset? On that note, we welcome you to the second match coverage of the Asia Cup 2025.
... MATCH DAY ...

The UAE has been cricket’s reliable friend and host for years now, from hosting the Champions Trophy earlier this year to the Asia Cup several times, and also the T20 World Cups previously. Consistently, it has delivered top-notch tournaments and memorable matches. The lavish city of Dubai gets to shine as it welcomes the Asia Cup 2025 for the first time, kicking off with an exciting Group A showdown between India and the hosts, the United Arab Emirates. It’s been quite a while since we’ve seen India in T20 action. Their last outing in the format was that dominant 4-1 series victory over England at home back in February. Before that, you’d have to rewind all the way to November 2024 and their tour of South Africa to find their previous away T20 assignment. Sure, the IPL happened in between, followed by a few domestic leagues, but international cricket brings its own unique pressures and dynamics that domestic leagues simply can’t replicate. Suryakumar Yadav leads the Indian side that has a good blend of experience and youth. All eyes will be on vice-captain Shubman Gill at the top of the order, especially after his stellar performances during that English summer, where he looked in sublime touch. The opening partner slot is where things get interesting. It’s essentially a toss-up between Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma, with current form likely to be the deciding factor. Word is that Abhishek might just have his nose ahead, but these are the kind of selection dilemmas that teams love to have. The middle order reads like a who’s who of power hitters, featuring players who’ve been backing themselves to come good after getting consistent opportunities. Then there’s Hardik Pandya, the seasoned campaigner who’ll anchor the all-rounder role. With Jadeja stepping away from T20Is, Hardik becomes the most experienced player in the squad, shouldering that crucial dual responsibility. The bowling attack gets a massive lift with Jasprit Bumrah's return to T20I action following that epic 2024 World Cup final. India’s premier fast bowler is expected back to doing what he does best, which is making batters’ lives absolutely miserable. Partnering with him is Arshdeep Singh, a bowler who flies under the radar, but his control and smart bowling make him a valuable asset, whether he’s operating with the new ball or handling those pressure-cooker death overs. Dubai’s conditions are expected to offer fresher, livelier surfaces that should make for entertaining cricket. However, the region has a reputation for producing slower tracks that naturally favour spin bowling, which could influence team selection in a big way. With Kuldeep Yadav spearheading the spin department, there’s a strong possibility we could see additional tweakers like Axar Patel and Varun Chakaravarthy getting the nod. Both bring different skill sets to the table and have proven themselves handy in these conditions. Facing them fearlessly are the hosts, the UAE. There’s plenty of talent in this squad, as glimpsed in the recently wrapped-up tri-series in Sharjah. Sure, the results didn’t fall their way, but the sparks of promise were hard to miss. Leading from the front is Muhammad Waseem - not just the skipper, but very much the spine of their batting unit. The middle order, though, carries a shade of inexperience, their most glaring vulnerability so far. This upcoming test will stretch them, and how they handle the pressure against stronger sides will define their fight. Death bowling has also been a concern, with pacers like Muhammad Jawadullah and Junaid Siddique needing to sharpen up if they are to hold their own in the closing stages. Surprisingly, these two teams have crossed paths only once before - all the way back in the 2016 Asia Cup in Mirpur. India took that one comfortably, but the landscape has shifted since. The Men in Blue still walk in as clear favourites, yet cricket has a way of tossing up the unexpected. Could the UAE carve out a shock or two in this Group A opener? All signs point to a thrilling clash under the lights at the Dubai International Stadium.
